key_insight: AI-optimized quantum measurements extract task-relevant information before photodetection, achieving exponentially lower discrimination error as photons accumulate than direct imaging or single-photon-optimized measurements.
engineering_relevance: Task-specific optical measurement design could improve photon-efficient machine vision in low-light and noisy sensing systems.
method: Train a diffractive optical neural network followed by a detector array.
Use a quantum information-theoretic objective to maximize the discrimination-error decay rate as photons accumulate.
Optimize the measurement to mitigate detector noise.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation in a noiseless setting and a photon-counting experiment using an electron-multiplying CCD, with noise corresponding to 10^4 photons per signal photon.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish how well task-specific measurements generalize to new visual tasks or changing noise conditions.
